answer: A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, as the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The canyon multiplier is published, charged in bridge, and inlet lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 12 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1202 identities would post 1259 proofs and burn roughly 16 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
